newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says 115,000 refugees in Zaire flee their camp.
newsitem.headline: UN says 115,000 refugees in Zaire flee their camp.

text.p: Some 115,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees fled their camp in east Zaire on Thursday after fighting and are heading south towards the world's most crowded refugee camp already sheltering 400,000 people, the U.N. refugee agency said.

UNHCR spokeswoman Ruth Marshall told Reuters in Geneva the camp of Kahindo, blanketting a mountain valley in the shadow of volcanoes some 60 km (38 miles) north of eastern Zaire's border town of Goma town, was now empty.
"Refugees started fleeing after two o'clock in the morning. As of mid-morning today (Thursday), the camp of Kahindo was empty," she said.
Marshall said the refugees, joined by some 20,000 local Zairean villagers, were heading towards the sprawling Mugunga camp already packed with 400,000 Hutus just outside Goma town.

Aid workers said they feared the fighting could set off yet another mass exodus from Katale camp, sheltering more than 200,000 Rwandan Hutus, near Kahindo camp. Marshall said there was no movement yet out of Katale.

On the edge of Goma town, Tutsi fighters and Zairean forces exchanged mortar and machinegun fire on Thursday and a U.N. spokesman said the Tutsi fighters captured Goma's airport, the centre for efforts to aid refugees.

The airport is about four km (2.5 miles) north of the city centre and a key target because aid agencies use it to bring in staff and supplies for refugees and the Zairean military has been bringing in army reinforcements in recent days through it.
Marshall said 14 UNHCR expatriate employees and another 86 staff members of Western aid agencies were trapped in Goma, which is already cut off from all aid routes.
Shelling and shooting in Kibumba camp north of Goma on Friday and Saturday prompted 200,000 refugees to flee to Mugunga, swelling its population to some 400,000.

Aid agencies are scrambling to prevent large loss of life from disease and hunger in Mugunga. The U.N. refugee agency says that it has no access to up to 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees around Goma and 300,000 more around Goma and Butare town.
